description.text: This entry represents FrsA esterase proteins, cutinases, hydrolases and related proteins. The FrsA family proteins are esterases that catalyse the hydrolysis of esters. Members of this family are involved in various biological processes, including the degradation of cutin, a plant cuticle polyester, and the hydrolysis of synthetic polyesters like poly(ethylene terephthalate), commonly known as PET. Some family members participate in complex biosynthetic pathways for natural products with biological activities, such as mycotoxin production, antibiotic properties, and cell cycle inhibition. The family includes proteins that can act as quorum-quenching agents, disrupting bacterial communication. Additionally, certain FrsA family proteins are implicated in fungal virulence and plant pathogenicity, with roles in melanin biosynthesis and the production of fungal signals recognised by resistant plants [[cite:PUB00104162]].

ec.description: ENZYME is a repository of information relative to the nomenclature of enzymes. It is primarily based on the recommendations of the Nomenclature Committee of the International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB) and it describes each type of characterized enzyme for which an EC (Enzyme Commission) number has been provided.
